title: Descent of maps between fixed bounded module families
statement: Let I be a directed preorder, R:I → CommRingCat a diagram of Noetherian rings, c a limit cone of its spectra with affine apex, i∈I, and f:Xi → Spec(Ri) a locally finitely presented qcqs morphism [def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Write X for its base change to c.pt [def-pc-base-change]. Fix j≥i and a finitely presented quasi-coherent family F_n on Xj [pqf-def-coherent], zero outside [a,b]. Given maps φ_n between their limit pullbacks in adjacent degrees, there exist k≥j (and k≥i), a finitely presented quasi-coherent family G_n on Xk zero outside [a,b], maps δ_n:G_n → G_(n+1), and isomorphisms t_n from the limit pullbacks of G_n to those of F_n such that pullback(δ_n) followed by t_(n+1) equals t_n followed by φ_n. No new arbitrary family on X is descended in this statement.

proof.text: Use induction on a finite set of integer degrees to construct a later stage, a bounded finitely presented quasi-coherent model family, arbitrary successive maps, and comparison isomorphisms commuting with the prescribed maps in exactly those selected degrees. For the empty set use the input family at its own stage, zero successive maps, and identity comparisons.

At an insertion n, conjugate the next desired map by the current comparisons and apply the map clause of finitePresentation_module_map_descent. Pull all existing models to its returned later stage, keeping their zero support and finite presentation. Pull the old maps as well, except in degree n, where the newly descended map is used. Compose the inverse of the returned natural comparison with each current term comparison. Multiplying the map-clause equation on either side by the inverse comparisons proves the new degree equation; inverse comparison naturality preserves every old degree equation.

Apply the finite-set assertion to Finset.Icc a (b-1). For each other n, integer arithmetic gives n<a or b<n+1. In the first case the limit pullback of the new source term is zero; in the second case the limit pullback of the old target term is zero. Equality of all maps with zero source or target yields the required compatibility. This includes boundary maps, empty intervals, and singleton intervals. Zero preservation uses nonempty_tensorPullbackAdjunction from the module-pullback node, not the separate canonical-unit adjunction theorem.

proof_origin.note: P3 complete Lean proof by finite-set induction. Each step uses one-map descent and inverse comparison naturality; no separate associativity coherence statement is used.

mathlib_searches.query: A bounded family of finitely presented quasicoherent sheaves descends to a stage of a directed limit of schemes
A finite family of finitely presented quasicoherent modules and maps descends along a directed affine inverse limit
mathlib_searches.results: Eight sheaf finite-presentation definitions and instances; no geometric family descent theorem.
Directed.finset_le supplies a common stage only; no family or sheaf-map descent theorem.

Affine graded scalar extension descent exists but assumes affine module categories, whereas Xi need not be affine. No scheme-module version; existing finitePresentation_module_map_descent supplies the one-object and one-map primitives.

theorem bounded_graded_map_compatibility
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (R : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) [∀ k : I, IsNoetherianRing (R.obj k)]
    (c : Cone (R.op ⋙ Scheme.Spec)) (hc : IsLimit c) [IsAffine c.pt]
    (i : I) {Xi : Scheme.{u}} (f : Xi ⟶ Spec (R.obj i))
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (a b : ℤ) (j : I) (hij : i ≤ j)
    (F : ℤ → (pullback f (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij)))).Modules)
    (hF_zero : ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (F n))
    (hF_fp : ∀ n : ℤ, (F n).IsFinitePresentation)
    (hF_qc : ∀ n : ℤ, (F n).IsQuasicoherent)
    (φ : ∀ n : ℤ, (Scheme.Modules.moduleBaseChange f
          (T := Over.mk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij))))
          (T' := Over.mk (c.π.app (op i)))
          (Over.homMk (c.π.app (op j)) (c.w (homOfLE hij).op))).obj (F n) ⟶
        (Scheme.Modules.moduleBaseChange f
          (T := Over.mk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij))))
          (T' := Over.mk (c.π.app (op i)))
          (Over.homMk (c.π.app (op j)) (c.w (homOfLE hij).op))).obj (F (n + 1))) :
    ∃ (k : I) (_hjk : j ≤ k) (hik : i ≤ k)
      (G : ℤ → (pullback f (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hik)))).Modules)
      (δ : ∀ n : ℤ, G n ⟶ G (n + 1)),
      (∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (G n)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, (G n).IsFinitePresentation) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, (G n).IsQuasicoherent) ∧
      ∃ t : ∀ n : ℤ, (Scheme.Modules.moduleBaseChange f
          (T := Over.mk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hik))))
          (T' := Over.mk (c.π.app (op i)))
          (Over.homMk (c.π.app (op k)) (c.w (homOfLE hik).op))).obj (G n) ≅
        (Scheme.Modules.moduleBaseChange f
          (T := Over.mk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij))))
          (T' := Over.mk (c.π.app (op i)))
          (Over.homMk (c.π.app (op j)) (c.w (homOfLE hij).op))).obj (F n),
        ∀ n : ℤ, (Scheme.Modules.moduleBaseChange f
          (T := Over.mk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hik))))
          (T' := Over.mk (c.π.app (op i)))
          (Over.homMk (c.π.app (op k)) (c.w (homOfLE hik).op))).map (δ n) ≫
          (t (n + 1)).hom = (t n).hom ≫ φ n
